chunks: And from his speech (peace be upon him), regarding the mention of the allegiance.
And therein he describes his companions at Siffin when they prolonged preventing him from fighting the people of Syria.

key_terms.أَهْلِ الشَّامِ: The people of Syria (referring to Muawiyah's forces)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about his companions' behavior during the Battle of Siffin?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) reflects on the psychological shift among his troops during the Battle of Siffin, where prolonged hesitation transformed into a reluctance to fight, ultimately leading to the arbitration (Tahkim). This passage underscores the pivotal moment when the desire for peace began to overshadow the commitment to decisive victory, a key theme in Shia historiography regarding the erosion of military resolve. The narration serves as a critical commentary on the internal dynamics of the early Islamic community and the political complexities of Ali's caliphate.
